# Copilot Instructions

Personal website built with Angular 22 and TypeScript 6.0 (zoneless, signals, prerendered to static HTML) and SCSS. Deployed to GitHub Pages via GitHub Actions.

## Commands

```bash
npm start            # dev server at http://localhost:4200
npm run build        # production build: regenerates build info, prerenders every route into dist/browser
npm test             # unit tests (Vitest, watch mode)
npm run test:ci      # unit tests, single run — what CI runs
npm run lint         # ESLint (TS + HTML)
npm run check        # lint + production build + test:ci, in that order
npm run layout       # after a build: every page × every size in Chrome (set CHROME_PATH outside CI)
```

**Single test file:**
```bash
ng test --include='src/app/home-page/home-page.component.spec.ts'
```

Tests run on Vitest with happy-dom; no browser is needed. Use Node 24 (`.nvmrc`; `nvm use`): its npm 11 installs Vitest 4.1, whose optional peer graph crashes npm 10 (`Cannot read properties of null (reading 'edgesOut')`), so `npm ci` on Node 22 fails. npm 11 blocks dependencies' install scripts unless `allowScripts` in `package.json` allows them; the four that have one (esbuild, lmdb, `@parcel/watcher`, msgpackr-extract) are recorded there as denied, since their prebuilt binaries make the scripts unnecessary. If a new dependency's script is reported, check whether it's needed before `npm install-scripts approve` (pinned). `overrides` lifts `@angular/build`'s pinned `vite` to a patched release; drop it when Angular catches up (`docs/ideas-later.md` §1).

**Versions:** TypeScript stays on the range `@angular/compiler-cli` accepts (`>=6.0 <6.1` for Angular 22); Dependabot ignores newer TypeScript until Angular does. Node is the current LTS, 24, set once in `.nvmrc` (CI and the deploy read it); `engines` is Angular's range minus 22 (`^24.15.0 || >=26`). The package `version` tracks the Angular major. Upgrade Angular with `ng update` (its migrations), not by bumping versions.

**CI** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, PRs into `master`): Lint and Test beside one production Build, then Lighthouse and Layout against that build's artifact. Those five job names are the required checks in the `master` ruleset, which also requires a PR (no approvals: the solo maintainer can't approve his own), blocks on high-severity CodeQL findings (default setup, weekly and on PRs) and asks Copilot for a review; merges are squash-only, and merged branches delete themselves. Dependabot (weekly, grouped) PRs for GitHub Actions merge themselves when green (`dependabot-auto-merge.yml`); npm ones wait for a person. Secret scanning and push protection are on. Workflows start from read-only (or no) permissions, check out with `persist-credentials: false`, and pin `npx` tools to exact versions; Dependabot waits 7 days after a release (security updates arrive at once). `SECURITY.md` says how to report a problem; the deploy writes `.well-known/security.txt` (with a rolling expiry) and uploads dot-folders for it. **Layout** (`scripts/check-layout.mjs`) loads every sitemap page at 360×740, 390×844, 740×360, 1024×768, 1440×900 and 2560×1080 in Chrome with third-party APIs blocked, and fails on sideways scroll (page or card), anything but one `<h1>`, tap targets under 44px on touch sizes (links inside a sentence excepted) or the ☾ overlapping the pager.

**Lighthouse CI** (the Lighthouse job, PRs only) audits every page in `public/sitemap.xml`, three runs each, as desktop and as a phone. Thresholds live in `lighthouserc.cjs`: accessibility or SEO below 0.95 fails, and so do the page-weight, JavaScript, image and layout-shift ceilings; performance and best-practices only warn. The ceilings are deliberately loose: they catch accidents, not drift. When something grows on purpose, raise the number. Scores land on the job's Summary page and as annotations (`scripts/lighthouse-summary.mjs`). The deploy also measures the homepage as a phone (`LH_PAGES=/`) and writes the median scores, weights and the ceilings above to `lighthouse.json` for the Lighthouse and Page weight badges on `/now` (both read it through `LighthouseReportService`). Then it runs the tests once more with coverage and `scripts/write-site-status.mjs` writes `site-status.json` for the Build badge: the commit's number (the deploy checks out full history for `git rev-list --count`), the merged PR's checks (CI only runs on PRs, so the merge commit has none of its own), tests and line coverage, and when a deploy last failed, using the job's own `GITHUB_TOKEN` (read-only `actions`, `checks`, `pull-requests`). Both steps are `continue-on-error` over committed placeholders in `public/`, so the badges hide everywhere else and nothing here can block a deploy. The deploy runs on every push to `master`, daily at 10:17 UTC (`schedule`) and from "Run workflow" (`workflow_dispatch`); the scheduled run redeploys `master` as it is, so the badges re-measure and the Letterboxd diary refreshes.

**Letterboxd** (`src/shared/letterboxd/`): Letterboxd's API isn't open to personal sites and its feed is CORS-blocked, so the deploy reads Morgan's public RSS feed (never the HTML) with `scripts/write-letterboxd.mjs` into `dist/browser/letterboxd.json`: his 50 most recent diary entries, lists dropped, no posters (the terms rule out in-line linking to them), reviews as plain text. If the feed fails it keeps the live site's copy, then the placeholder `public/letterboxd.json`, so the diary hides rather than blanks; the step is `continue-on-error`. `letterboxd.ts` is the one parser and validator for both sides: the script imports it straight from Node 24 (type stripping), so it stays import-free and erasable-only (no enums, no parameter properties), and the browser checks the JSON again with `toDiary`. Everything that shows the diary reads `LetterboxdService` (`diary`, `latest`). Ratings render through `app-stars` (`src/shared/stars/`): gold stars hidden from screen readers, the rating in words beside them.

## Architecture

```
src/
  app/               # Page components (one folder per route)
    app.config.ts            # providers: zoneless, router + view transitions, hydration, HTTP
    app.config.server.ts     # server providers for prerendering
    app.routes.ts            # lazy route table, built from MAIN_ROUTES
    app.routes.server.ts     # RenderMode.Prerender for everything
  shared/            # Reusable components, directives, services, styles
    base-page/       # Shell: the glass page card + navbar (+ optional visually-hidden <h1>)
    page-header/     # <app-page-header>: a page's visible h1, dim one-liner, optional meta
    custom-navbar/   # Navigation: one line on wide screens, a pager on tablets/phones; links from MAIN_ROUTES
    icon/            # <app-icon name="…">: the site's few glyphs as inline SVG
    vertical-nav/    # Interests tiles: a [preview] slot while collapsed, ↑/↓ + Enter/Esc, one section expanded at a time
    scroll-region/   # ScrollRegionService + [appScrollRegion] for arrow-key scrolling
    config/site.config.ts    # every handle, URL and endpoint the site uses
    services/        # KeyboardNavService, SeoTitleStrategy, ApiCacheService, API clients
    sky/             # Tonight's sky: live canvas behind every page (see below)
    badges/          # The 88×31 buttons on /now: the app-badge shell, one small component per badge
    route-transition.ts  # View Transitions direction logic
    main-routes.ts       # the main pages: path, title, description
    shared-styles.scss   # Shared mixins: surface, panel, band, panel-grid, prose, label, progress-bar, scrollbar-styled
  styles.scss        # Global styles, color variables, route-transition CSS
public/              # static assets, robots.txt, sitemap.xml, humans.txt, site.webmanifest, data/sky/
scripts/             # build-info (prebuild hook); deploy-time badge data; sky data, landscape and 88×31 generators (one-off)
art/                 # source art (the painting, lossless); not served
```

**Page structure:** Each route has its own folder under `src/app/<name>-page/`. Pages import `BasePageComponent` to get the navbar. Complex pages may contain nested sub-components in subfolders (e.g. `interests-page/osrs-stats/` is one data-fetching parent plus one small component per panel).

**Routing:** Main routes are declared once in `MAIN_ROUTES` (`src/shared/main-routes.ts`) with a `path`, `title` and `description`. Their order drives arrow-key navigation (`KeyboardNavService`), the navbar, slide direction, titles and meta tags. `src/app/app.routes.ts` maps each path to a lazy `loadComponent` via `lazyRouteComponents` and derives `data.animation` / `data.description` from the route. Don't hand-write `animation` values.

**Adding a page:** add the entry to `MAIN_ROUTES`, add its loader to `lazyRouteComponents` in `app.routes.ts` (the `MainRoutePath` type fails the build if you forget), add the URL to `public/sitemap.xml` (a test fails if you forget; Lighthouse CI picks the page up from there), and give the page a header: `<app-page-header title="…" description="…">` inside `<app-base-page>` (or a visually-hidden h1 when the page shows its title another way: `<app-base-page pageTitle="…">`, or its own as Interests does while a section is open). Exactly one `<h1>` per page. The navbar and pager update themselves.

**Build info:** `npm run build` runs `scripts/write-build-info.mjs` first (the `prebuild` hook), writing the gitignored `src/build-info.prod.ts` that the production configuration swaps in for `src/build-info.ts`. Always build production through `npm run build`; a bare `ng build` skips the hook and fails on the missing file.

**Prerendering:** every route is rendered to static HTML at build time (`outputMode: "static"`, `RenderMode.Prerender`) and hydrated in the browser. Code that touches `window`/`document` outside an event handler must be guarded (`typeof window !== 'undefined'`, `isPlatformServer`, or `afterNextRender`). Anything shown on first paint must be deterministic so hydration matches (e.g. the greeting picks its random subtitle after render). `ApiCacheService` returns `EMPTY` on the server and the HTTP transfer cache is disabled, so live panels are always fetched live in the browser. Hydration is Angular 22's default (incremental); the only `@defer` block is the name-a-star panel (`when` it's opened, so the server renders nothing for it), so everything else hydrates at once as before. Keep `withEventReplay()` explicit in `app.config.ts` so clicks before hydration aren't lost, even where it looks redundant.

**Tonight's sky** (`src/shared/sky/`): `app-sky` sits inside `App`'s `.canvas` div, over the painted `public/background.webp` (first paint and fallback), and draws the real sky with the painting in front at device resolution (capped at 2×; `layout.artPixel` = CSS px per buffer px). Layers, back to front: a sky canvas (the component paints the gradient and horizon glow with canvas gradients; `sky-render.ts` draws stars, lines and the Moon into a transparent RGBA buffer laid over it, pure and tested like `sky-math.ts`; then the halos), free look's panorama (`.free`, only while looking up), the Sun (a `.sun` element, so it can move), a landscape canvas, the hover overlay (`.overlay`, so hover never redraws the sky), then CSS for the farmhouse window, the campfire beside it and the dusk fireflies (`sky-landscape.ts` places them; `--night-light` and `--fireflies` on the host set how bright; all still under reduced motion). The sky and landscape canvases come in pairs: changing the light draws the new one once onto the hidden pair and crossfades to it over `TRANSITION_MS` while the Sun travels to its new place (`sky-transition.ts`), so a frame is only an opacity and a transform; never redraw the canvases per frame (it's heavy at 2× and crashed headless Chromium's software GPU). A change part way through folds the fade into the lower canvas and carries on; under reduced motion the light changes at once. `sky-bodies.ts` wraps `astronomy-engine`, which is only ever loaded with a dynamic `import()`. The landscape is `public/landscape/<look>.webp` (darkness, sunrise, sunset, day; 1920×1279, soft alpha), built by `scripts/build-landscape.py` from `art/painting.png` (soft matte, relighting, sunrise fog); `sky-landscape.ts` decides how much of each look to use. Star, name and constellation data are committed JSON in `public/data/sky/`, generated by `scripts/build-sky-data.mjs` from d3-celestial (a git checkout or `npm pack d3-celestial`): `names.json` is the bright named stars the hover labels use (mag ≤ 3), `proper-names.json` every proper name down to the catalogue's mag 4.5 (only name-a-star reads it). Nothing draws until the star data and the darkness look have loaded; if either fails the painting stays (if only astronomy-engine fails, the sky draws without the Moon and planets). Other looks load when first needed; a change of light waits up to 1.5 s for its look, then goes ahead with the darkness look standing in. `SkyService` holds whose sky it is and how it's lit (`Lighting`: `darkness` by default, then `real`, `sunrise`, `sunset`, `day`; staged sunrise/sunset put the Sun in the valley at `BACKGROUND_VALLEY`). Both are chosen in `app-sky-menu` (top-right ☾) and remembered in `localStorage`; only its "show my sky" button (`app-sky-toggle`) may call geolocation. Hovering or tapping open sky names what's there (`sky-hover.ts`; `HOVER_BLOCKERS` lists what blocks it — add a selector there if new content should; `app-sky-look-up` is there). The menu's "up right now" list (`sky-up-now.ts`) is the text equivalent of the canvas. **Look up** (☾ menu → "look up"): `SkyService.lookingUp` fades `App`'s `<main>` out (400 ms, instant under reduced motion) and makes it `inert` and `visibility: hidden`, so the whole window is sky and hover works anywhere; `app-sky-look-up` shows a fixed "‹ back to the page" pill bottom-left and listens for Escape on the document (innermost first: an open ☾ menu, then the naming panel, then look-up itself, each `preventDefault`ed so the site-wide Escape doesn't fire); any `NavigationStart` (← →, links) leaves it. Document-level key handlers that act on the page must skip it while it's inert (`KeyboardNavService`'s ↑/↓ scrolling and the Interests tiles check `closest('[inert]')`). While looking up, `App`'s `.canvas` comes in front of the hidden page (`z-index: 1`, once the page's 400 ms fade is done; at once under reduced motion) so the sky gets the pointer; looking up also closes the ☾ menu, and ↑/↓ on the hidden greeting do nothing. **Free look** (while looking up): the sky can be dragged all the way round (past north) and up to the zenith; the painting (landscape, Sun, window, campfire, fireflies) stays put and the sky turns behind it. The whole sky is drawn once into a panorama (`sky-panorama.ts`: a cylinder at the normal view's scale where they meet, due south on the horizon; 360° plus a screen's width across, so any facing is one unbroken stretch; running on past the zenith into the sky behind you, upside down; at most `MAX_PANORAMA_PIXELS` and 4096 px a side (wider textures fall back to software on some mobile GPUs), so big or dense screens get fewer buffer pixels per CSS pixel; its `ImageData` is made for each render and dropped straight after, so it costs its canvas, about 17–21 MB, and nothing in the JS heap between renders) by the same `renderSky`, which draws through a `SkyProjection` (`layoutProjection` for the normal view). **A drag, a glide or a turn only changes the panorama canvas's CSS transform; never redraw it per frame.** It's redrawn when the sky is (once a minute, on a change of light or place, on resize; a minute's tick or a resize during a drag, glide or turn waits until the sky comes to rest), and meanwhile the sky canvas carries only the gradient. Entering and leaving crossfade it with the normal view's stars over `TRANSITION_MS` (in the light transition's own frames; the stars on the way out go in the first 40%, so the two projections are barely seen together); leaving lets its memory go once faded, and free look always starts facing south (`SkyService.view`, never stored). `sky-free-look.ts` (pointer events with capture and `touch-action: none` on the sky, a press that moves under `TAP_SLOP` px is a tap and the click a drag ends with is swallowed, a gentle glide after a flick, none under reduced motion) and `sky-panorama.ts` load with the first look up; `sky-view.ts` (facing, tilt, the compass reading) is small and in main. Free look is on only once it has loaded and the sky has drawn (`SkyService.freeLooking`): until then there's no compass, no `cursor: grab` and no `touch-action: none`, and a turn asked for before it is dropped. `app-sky-compass` (top-left, first in the focus order; one row on short screens) reads "facing NNW · 338° · looking up 40°" and has 44px buttons to turn 45°, tilt 15° and face south, which go through `SkyService.turn`/`tilt`/`faceSouth` (`viewRequest`; the sky animates there, or jumps under reduced motion) and say where they leave you in a polite live region (so does a ‹ › turn, once it arrives; a drag says nothing); no arrow keys. Hover, tap-to-pick and the ring all map through the panorama and the current view. **Name a star**: "name a star" looks up with `app-star-naming` open. Candidates are stars in `stars.json` with no proper name in `proper-names.json` (same star = within 0.01° RA and Dec; 543 of the 921) and no visitor name, above the horizon, on screen, visible in the light, and not behind the landscape, the panel, the compass or the ☾ menu; "near X" is the nearest star the hover labels name (`names.json`), by angular separation, and the panel's count is the unnamed stars that ever rise at the sky's latitude (428 over Cincinnati). ‹ › go round every unnamed star above the horizon, on screen or not, by azimuth (from the selected star, or from the facing), and the sky turns as little as it can to bring each into view (`bringIntoView`: the same tilt turned to the first clear spot from the middle out, else tilted so it's half way up); stars no view can show clear of the landscape, the panel and the compass (low ones, especially under a phone's bottom sheet: tilting only moves a star down) are passed over (`SkyService.showable`), giving up after one lap. The pure logic (candidates, nearest named star, nearest-to-a-click, ‹ › order, the message) is `sky-naming.ts`, tested like `sky-math.ts`. The sky component works the candidates out after each draw, when the panel opens and when the ☾ menu opens or closes (`SkyService.candidates`, CSS px), selects the brightest only when nothing is selected (a selection stays while its star is above the horizon and on screen, so nothing changes under someone typing), lets a click on open sky pick the nearest within 24 px (36 px when the last `pointerdown` was touch), and puts a gold `.star-ring` element on the selected star (never drawn on the sky canvases; placed by a transform, it follows the star on every redraw and every frame of a turn). When the panel first appears it re-picks a star it now covers. The panel is `@defer`red until first opened, and binds plain inputs to signals rather than importing `FormsModule` (which would otherwise ride along with App); one permanent `role="status"` region carries its sent and error messages. The panel POSTs to `SITE_CONFIG.askMorganSubmitUrl` with `question` (the text Morgan's Discord gets, ending in an `approve:` line), `username_honey`, and `kind`/`name`/`credit`/`star`, which morganvanv.com-backend PR #1 (`feat/submission-kinds`) turns into a per-kind Discord embed with the `approve:` row in a code block. **Visitor names** live in `public/data/sky/visitor-names.json` (`[raDeg, decDeg, name, namedBy|null, "YYYY-MM"]`, hand-edited; `build-sky-data.mjs` refuses to write it; a spec fails if any row wouldn't parse). To approve a suggestion, paste its `approve:` row into `names` in a PR. The file loads with the other sky data but is optional: missing, broken or malformed rows just mean fewer names. Each becomes a hover target ("Gerald · named by sam, Oct 2026") and a line in the ☾ menu's "named by visitors" group ("Gerald · near Vega · by sam"; hidden while the list is empty), which is its text equivalent. `?sky-at=<ISO>` pins the time and `?sky-light=<lighting>` forces a lighting. `app-sky` sets `--daylight` (0 at night, 1 in daylight) on `<html>`; anything with text over the sky should darken with it, as `base-page`'s card does. To change the landscape, edit `scripts/build-landscape.py` and rerun it; never hand-edit the webps. If the painting's composition changes, check `BACKGROUND_SIZE` / `BACKGROUND_HORIZON_Y` / `BACKGROUND_VALLEY` / `BACKGROUND_WINDOW` / `BACKGROUND_CAMPFIRE` in `sky-render.ts`.

**SEO:** `SeoTitleStrategy` (registered as the router `TitleStrategy`) sets `Page · morganvanv.com`, the route description, Open Graph/Twitter tags, the canonical link and a JSON-LD `Person`. Site-wide defaults live in `index.html`. Canonical URLs and the sitemap use trailing slashes because GitHub Pages serves prerendered routes as directories.

## Conventions

**Design pillar — night is home:** the site is dark by default and designed against a night sky first. Anything brighter (daylight, sunrise, a light variant) is an opt-in the visitor chooses, never the landing state. When "accurate" and "looks like night" conflict, default to night and offer accuracy as a setting. New UI must still be readable if a visitor opts into a brighter sky.

**Design pillar — cultivate an atmosphere:** set a vibe and reward people for noticing it. Small flavor and easter eggs (a light left on in the farmhouse after dark, a campfire beside it, the Moon in its real phase) are worth building. Keep them quiet and discoverable, never in the way, never at the cost of accessibility.


**Standalone components:** All components are standalone. Never use NgModule. Do **not** set `standalone: true`.

**Zoneless + signals:** `provideZonelessChangeDetection()` is on; there is no zone.js. Components use `ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush` (the v22 default; still write it explicitly, and never use `Eager`), hold state in `signal()`/`computed()`, read observables with `toSignal()` or `AsyncPipe`, and never call `markForCheck()`. Use `input()` / `input.required()` and `host: { … }` metadata, never `@Input`, `@Output` or `@HostListener`. In tests, prefer `await fixture.whenStable()` to `fixture.detectChanges()`.

**Dependency injection:** Use `inject()` — not constructor injection.
```ts
private myService = inject(MyService);
```
For navigation, prefer `routerLink` over imperative `Router.navigate()` whenever possible.

**Icons:** `<app-icon name="chevron-down" />`. Add a path to `ICON_PATHS` in `src/shared/icon/icon.component.ts` for a new glyph. No icon fonts, no Angular Material.

**Fonts:** JetBrains Mono and Caveat are bundled from `@fontsource` (latin subsets, listed in `angular.json` `styles`). Never add a Google Fonts `<link>`; the build must not need the network.

**Keyboard:** ← → always page between routes (`KeyboardNavService`), Escape returns to the greeting, ↑/↓ scroll or move within a page. Don't give a widget arrow-key semantics that fight that: use toggle buttons with `aria-pressed` rather than ARIA tabs or radio groups (Music's top lists and Favorite Media's shelves do, styled by the `shared.toggle-group` / `shared.toggle-button` mixins), and ↑/↓ walk the Interests tiles in reading order even when they sit two across. Navigation UI marks the current/hovered item with the gold `[ ]` brackets (navbar, pager, tiles, the greeting's way in), reserving their space so nothing shifts.

**Badges (88×31 buttons):** they live in the Buttons panel at the bottom of `/now`, in two labelled rows in Morgan's order (the `/now` spec pins it): **tonight** — Cincinnati weather, Moon, Up tonight; **this site** — the site's own 88×31, Made with Angular, No cookies, Page weight, Lighthouse, Build; under them a **webring** row with Hotline Webring's ‹ prev / next › links (`SITE_CONFIG.webring`; never `rel="noreferrer"`, the ring learns members from the Referer). Each row keeps a badge's height while its live badges load, so nothing below shifts. Every badge renders through `app-badge` (`src/shared/badges/badge/`), which owns the look: 132×46 (1.5×), a glyph cell, a tiny gold caps name over the value, the classic bevel, a gold border on hover/focus, and a solid popover: shown for a real pointer (`hover: hover`) or keyboard focus, never after a tap; it stays while the pointer is on it and Escape hides it (WCAG 1.4.13) without triggering the site-wide Escape; it opens left near the right edge and below near the top, and is `display: none` until wanted so it can't widen the page. A badge is a small component with `:host { display: contents }` that works out its data and renders one `app-badge`, or nothing while it has no data; give it `href` (new tab), `route` (in-site) or neither (a button, `(pressed)`), a `label` with the full text that starts with the name on its face (the face is tiny, the popover is `aria-hidden`, and voice control matches the visible name), and an inline-SVG glyph coloured with the `glyph.colors` classes (`src/shared/badges/_glyph.scss`). Data must be real or the joke must be true, and nothing may need tending or block a deploy. The Moon and Up tonight badges read the sky's own numbers (`SkyService.upNow().detail`, so `?sky-at=` moves them too) and open the ☾ menu with `SkyService.openMenu()`; Weather (Open-Meteo, Cincinnati), Lighthouse and Page weight (`/lighthouse.json`, shared through `LighthouseReportService`) and Build (`/site-status.json`) read their data with `cachedJson(url, ttl, parse)` (`src/shared/services/cached-json.ts`): a cached GET as a signal that stays null until valid data arrives, so a failure just hides the badge. Each badge's spec sits beside it. Shelved for now, in `docs/ideas-later.md`: Photo Wall, Vinyl Collection, Under construction. The site's own button is `public/88x31.gif`, drawn by `scripts/build-88x31.py`; keep it and its HTML twin in `own-button-badge` in step.

**Favorite Media** (`src/app/interests-page/favorite-media/`): the wall is hand-picked and only that: `FAVORITE_MEDIA` in `src/shared/constants/favorite-media.const.ts`, in wall order, up to four per shelf (Films, TV, Books, Albums; a test holds them to four, a short shelf keeps blank slots so its row stays even, an empty shelf hides). Shelves sit two across on wide screens, four covers to a row; one shelf at a time on tablets and phones (2×2 on phones). A card is a cover, a title, who made it (`by`: authors and artists, required for books and albums) and a short blurb if Morgan writes one, in the site's mono. Covers are committed `public/media/<id>.webp`, 400×600 (albums square, 400×400), made by `python3 scripts/build-media-covers.py <folder of originals named by id>` (originals stay out of the repo); then set `cover` on the pick, and the wall's spec checks each file exists at its size and none is orphaned; without one the card sets the title in type, scaled to the cover. Blurbs are Morgan's words, never drafted. The Letterboxd diary is a separate feed under the wall (`letterboxd-diary/`), and the collapsed tile previews the last film watched (`media-preview/`).

**Scroll regions:** Put `appScrollRegion` on the element arrow keys should scroll (`[appScrollRegion]="false"` withdraws it). The innermost registered region wins.

**Config:** External handles, usernames, URLs and the Ask Morgan endpoint live in `SITE_CONFIG` (`src/shared/config/site.config.ts`). API clients go through `ApiCacheService.get(url, ttlMs?)` (sessionStorage, 10-minute TTL by default; `0` bypasses the cache); to read one as a signal that's null until valid data arrives, use `cachedJson(url, ttlMs, parse)`. `provideHttpClient()` uses Fetch by default since Angular 22: don't add the deprecated `withFetch()`, and only add `withXhr()` if something needs upload progress. In tests, `provideHttpClient()` + `provideHttpClientTesting()` is enough.

**Contact form** (`src/app/home-page/ask-morgan-form/`): three jobs as toggle buttons (ask me something, suggest a subtitle, anonymous dropbox), each keeping its own draft. Everything posts to the Ask Morgan function, which forwards to Morgan's Discord. The payload's `question` is always a complete human-readable message (the deployed function reads only `question` and the honeypot), with `kind` and structured fields beside it (`contact-submission.ts`). The greeting's lines live in `src/shared/constants/subtitles.const.ts`: Morgan's in `SUBTITLES` (the first is prerendered), approved visitors' in `GUEST_SUBTITLES`, shown with a handwritten Caveat credit. A suggestion arrives with an `approve:` line; approving it means pasting that line into `GUEST_SUBTITLES` in a PR.

**Live data that must stay fresh** (anything a visitor would notice going stale) polls from a root service while the tab is visible — see `RecentStreamService` for the pattern (`visibilitychange` + `timer`, `switchMap` to the fetch, errors → `null`, nothing rendered). Components only read its signals.

**Component metadata style:** Use `styleUrl` (singular) and `templateUrl`. Imports should have spaces after `{`. Top-level page components follow the `*.component.ts/html/scss` naming convention. Sub-components may omit the `.component.` infix — both patterns exist.
```ts
@Component({
  selector: 'app-my-page',
  imports: [BasePageComponent],
  templateUrl: './my-page.component.html',
  styleUrl: './my-page.component.scss',
  changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush,
})
```

**SCSS — global variables:** Import and use the global color variables and breakpoint rather than hardcoding values.
```scss
@use '../../styles' as *;
// Available: $background-color, $background-sky-color, $main-color, $accent-color, $osrs-gold, $danger-color,
// breakpoints ($breakpoint-phone/-mobile/-short/-wide), card/navbar tokens, and the $font-size-* scale
```
A `--accent-color` CSS custom property is also set on `body` for inline template styles.

**Data-driven lists:** Use typed arrays in the component class + `@for` loops for any repeated structural elements.

**Page layout (the face-lift system):** every page is a compact header (`<app-page-header>`), an optional full-width band (`shared.band`: the h-card, now playing, the OSRS character), then panels (`shared.panel` + `shared.panel-heading`) laid out with `shared.panel-grid(<columns>)`, which stacks them on tablets and phones. Reading text uses `shared.prose`; gold caps labels use `shared.label`. Type comes from the `$font-size-*` scale in `styles.scss` (fixed rem, not tied to window height). The page card is 90% of the window up to `$card-max-width` (the painting stays visible around it) and `$card-inset-mobile` from the edges on tablets and phones; `base-page`'s `.page-content` is the one scroll container, so pages shouldn't add their own unless a panel needs it.

**SCSS — shared utilities:** Cards use `@include shared.surface` (dark fill + faint border) or `shared.panel` (surface + padding/radius), with `shared.panel-heading` for a title + dim qualifier; bars use `shared.progress-bar`; anchors use `shared.band`; text uses `shared.prose` / `shared.label`; side-by-side panels use `shared.panel-grid`. Use `@include shared.scrollbar-styled` in any scrollable container's SCSS. Import it with `@use '../../shared/shared-styles.scss' as shared;`. Sub-components that should lay out as if they were their parent's flex item use `:host { display: contents; }`.

**SCSS — breakpoints:** Use the named breakpoints, never raw px: `$breakpoint-mobile` (1000px, `max-width`: tablets and phones get the pager navbar and one-column layouts), `$breakpoint-phone` (600px, `max-width`: phone-only tweaks such as 2-up walls), `$breakpoint-short` (500px, `max-height`: landscape phones) and `$breakpoint-wide` (1600px, where the card stops growing). Pages must work from 360×740 to 2560×1080, including 740×360, with no horizontal scroll and ≥ 44px tap targets.

**Navbar and ☾:** on tablets and phones the navbar is a pager (greeting, ‹ previous, `[ current ]` opening the page list, next ›) whose right end is left free; `app-sky-menu` is fixed over that slot at those sizes, so the ☾ reads as one of its buttons. Keep the two in step if either moves.

**Global layout:** `body` has `overflow: hidden` globally (no page-level scroll); `base-page`'s `.page-content` scrolls. Body type is `$font-size-body` (1rem); pills (`.pill`) size with the text around them (`0.9em`).

**Motion:** Route changes use the View Transitions API (`withViewTransitions` + `onViewTransitionCreated` in `route-transition.ts`; CSS in `styles.scss`). `@angular/animations` is not a dependency; use CSS. Everything decorative must respect `prefers-reduced-motion` (a global rule covers CSS animations; JS-driven motion such as the 3D model's auto-rotate and the sky's light changes checks `matchMedia`).

**Images:** compressed `.webp` in `public/` with real `alt` (or `alt=""` when decorative), and `width`/`height` attributes where the CSS doesn't already fix the box. Encode from the lossless original (history has them, e.g. the Ada collage's PNG in `cfa9dd2`), never from an already-compressed copy; offer a larger `srcset` variant when the image is shown big. Give list and off-screen images `loading="lazy"`, and always inside a collapsed Interests section: content projected into `app-vertical-nav-item` is created even while collapsed, so an eager `<img>` there downloads on the landing page (the Music covers cost 3 MB until #89). `og-image.jpg` (link previews don't all support webp) and `88x31.gif` (other sites paste it into old-web pages) are the deliberate non-webps.

**ESLint rules:** Component selectors must use `app-` prefix in kebab-case; directive selectors must use `app` prefix in camelCase. The house conventions are lint rules too, so they're checked rather than remembered: explicit OnPush, signal-based inputs/queries (`readonly`), `output()`, built-in control flow (`@if`/`@for`), `type` on every `<button>`, and self-closing tags for empty elements (`npx eslint --fix` handles most).

**Formatting:** no formatter; `.editorconfig` sets the basics (2 spaces, LF, single quotes in TS) and ESLint's stylistic rules do the rest.
